overall: The AG found the Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law on both counts: it mishandled an executive session minutes request and failed to hold a roll call vote to enter executive session. It ordered the minutes amended and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to respond properly to a request for executive session minutes; it decided not to release them but did not communicate that promptly.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that, while the Board performed the required review of the requested minutes within the timeframe required by law, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to properly respond to the request.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly did not take a roll call vote before entering executive session; the minutes recorded only a voice tally of '3 ayes'.
allegations.key_passage: This does not satisfy the Open Meeting Law's requirement that public bodies record a roll call vote before convening in executive session.

remedy: Amend the minutes of the December 17, 2014 meeting to reflect a roll call vote.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order the Board to amend the minutes of the December 17, 2014 meeting to reflect a roll call vote. We also order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
